questions.q: What does the summary call both Google's greatest strength and weakness?
a: It crowdsources its answers
It updates its results too slowly
It charges for the best information
It relies on a single expert per topic
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Google's crowdsourced answers are its biggest advantage and also its biggest flaw.

questions.q: Why might a crowd give worse advice than one trained expert?
a: Popular answers may not suit every person's situation
Crowds are usually less educated than experts
Experts are required by law to be accurate
Crowds take much longer to reach a conclusion
questions.why: Lesson 1 says top answers may have worked for many people without necessarily working for all people.

questions.q: What does Plato say about schooling for children?
a: It cannot be identical for every child
It should begin with philosophy and logic
It must be led by certified experts only
It should stop once basic literacy is reached
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes Plato's line that since every child differs, education cannot be the same for all.

questions.q: Once a foundation is laid, what should education do?
a: Adapt to each person's talents and needs
Focus on preparing students for one career
Standardize lessons across every school
Emphasize memorization over exploration
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that after the groundwork, teaching has to fit individual talents, skills and needs.

questions.q: How does Plato define love in the summary?
a: As the base of all relationships, at varying intimacy
As romance kept separate from friendship
As a feeling reserved for couples
As an emotion that excludes rational thought
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Plato saw love as all-encompassing and present in every human relationship.
